long_biography.plain_text:
A graduate of the Stockholm School of Economics, Dahlberg began investing in small technology-intensive businesses during the 1990s. His early portfolio included QlikTech, while later investments concentrated on medical technology, life science and novel materials. Rather than acting as a passive shareholder, he combined capital with decades-long board mandates.

At Corline Biomedical, Dahlberg has served as chairman while the company develops heparin-based technologies for transplantation and cell therapy. He is also Senzime's vice-chairman and remains a director of Acuvi, extending the same patient-capital approach across patient monitoring and precision-motion systems. Agriculture, forestry and real estate form additional interests but not the core of his public investment identity.
